submitted.rationale: Index 24 (Cu0.135 Sb0.865) had the highest EQE of the three measured: 0.00286 %. That is about 7x index 15 (CuSb2O6, 0.00041 %) and about 40x index 5 (Cu-rich, 0.000069 %). EQE rose steadily toward the Sb-rich end, so the Sb-rich CuSb2O6 + Sb-oxide region performs best.

rejected.reason: Stoichiometric CuSb2O6 (on the MACE hull) measured 0.00041 % EQE, about 7x lower than index 24
Cu-rich; MACE puts Cu2SbO5 1.16 eV/atom above the hull, so this is likely a CuO + CuSb2O6 mixture; lowest EQE, 0.000069 %

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts CuSb2O6 (trirutile) on the hull, so index 15 (Cu 0.346, nearest 1:2) should be phase-pure CuSb2O6. The MEGNet HSE gap of ~0 eV looks like an artifact for Cu2+ d9; the experimental gap is ~2 eV, below 2.7 eV. Measuring the stable ternary phase first.

Mixed: MACE finds Cu2SbO5 far above the hull (1.16 eV/atom), so index 5 is probably a CuO + CuSb2O6 mixture and not a new ternary phase. Index 15, the CuSb2O6 end, gave very low EQE (4e-4 %), so the Cu-rich side is the main region left to test. I am measuring it to cover the other half of the composition line.

Weak support: MEGNet puts Sb2O5 at ~1.8 eV, but that value is not reliable. EQE went up about 6x from Cu-rich (idx 5) to CuSb2O6 (idx 15). Extending that trend points to the Sb-rich CuSb2O6 + Sb-oxide region, so I am using the last measurement there.
